When injured, starving, or stressed, it can revert its adult medusa form back to its juvenile polyp stage, essentially resetting its life cycle.

Those polyps then bud off new jellyfish that are genetically identical to the original. In theory, this cycle could repeat indefinitely, making it functionally “immortal” until something kills it.
